# Overview

## Introduction
This document describes how to make use of the Fudo API. In order to use
the API, you must first have created an account in Fudo.

You can access the openapi spec yaml file
[here](https://api.fu.do/v1alpha1/openapi.yml).

## Authentication
Authentication is through an access token, sending the token in each
request within the `Authorization` header. In order to obtain the token,
you must first have the access credentials `apiKey` and `apiSecret`.

### Access credentials
If you do not yet have an `apiKey` and `apiSecret`, write to soporte@fu.do
indicating the name of the account in Fudo and the user of the account to
which you want to give API access.

We recommend creating a user especially for API access , in order to keep
regular system users separated from users used for API access. E.g.
api@mirestaurante. Keep in mind that the actions that can be done through
the API will depend on the role assigned to the user associated to the
token.

### Obtaining the token
To obtain the token, a request must be sent to the authentication endpoint
with the access credentials. It is important to send the `Content-Type`
header as `application/json`.

The authentication endpoint is `https://auth.fu.do/api`.

Example:

```terminal
curl -X POST https://auth.fu.do/api \
     -d '{"apiKey":"123456","apiSecret":"654321"}' \
     -H "Accept: application/json" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json"
```

As a response, the access token will be obtained.

```json
{"token":"1234567890", exp: "1645387452"}
```

The returned token will be the one that must be sent later in each request
made to the API, within the `Authorization` header, prefixed with the
`Bearer` value, for example, `Authorization: Bearer 1234567890`.

### Token expiration
The token lasts for 24 hours, after this time it can no longer be used and
a new token must be obtained. The expiration date is included in the `exp`
attribute in the json response as an integer number of seconds since the
Epoch.

This makes possible to know in advance when the token will expire and to
renew it if it has already expired at the time of using it again, or the
expiration date is approaching.

## Pagination
Most of the endpoints for retrieving collections (customers, sales, etc.)
accept two query params for indicating the number of items to return (page
size) and the current page number (offset).

- `page[size]`
- `page[number]`

By default, the page size is 250 and the default page number is 1.

Currently, there is no way to get the total number of items. The way to get
all the items is to keep doing requests until the number of items received
is lower than the page size. That indicates there are no more items to
retrieve.

The max items allowed per page is 500. In order to minimize the number of
request it is possible to send this max value in the `size` param instead
of using the default.

E.g:

```
https://api.fu.do/v1alpha1/sales?page[size]=500&page[number]=2
```
